comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: I worked in Saudi Arabia in the late 1990s (SW, Khamis Mushayt and Abha) I will never forget tramping about on the edge of the escarpment. I used to go into the desert and often found open structures like caves on natural needle-like natural stone formations. with wonderful views and sometimes rock paintings. But once a bedouin boy was following me around. We started talking, and he thought a moment and told me to follow him. I couldn’t believe what I was seeing. A huge cave facing east, protected from the occasional monsoon rains and preserved by the dry desert air. A profusion of dozens of larger than life paintings. Stags with great antlers, camels and wild animals being hunted. As we proceeded, there were negative relief pictures, unpainted. Then came a new series of pictures, but this time the camels were being ridden. The conclusions were: 1. this area was once much wetter 2. we are seeing the transition from the camel as a wild animal to the domestication of camels in a historic panorama. There was no writing. I spoke with someone at Cambridge, who told me that when people can write, they write, so the pictures predate the introduction of writing and had not yet been seen in the modern time by Arabs who could write. Saudi back then was open only to people with work permits, there was no tourism like now. Listening to your video, particularly about the pictures in Tassili Ajjer, brings back the feeling of wonder and astonishment I had then. I thought Augustine was Roman and came from Tunisia. Wrong, he was Berber and came from Algeria!

comments.author: @BoydXplorer
comments.text:
Algeria is the largest country in Africa, stretching from a lush, mountainous Mediterranean coastline in the north deep into the vast, dramatic expanses of the Sahara Desert in the south. It is a land of striking contrasts, rich history, and deep cultural heritage. A narrow, fertile coastal strip along the Mediterranean Sea where the capital, Algiers, and the vast majority of the population reside. Tell Atlas and Saharan Atlas are parallel ranges running east-to-west, dividing the coast from the interior plateaus.The Sahara Desert covering over 80% of the country, featuring massive sand dunes (ergs), rocky plateaus, and the dramatic volcanic peaks of the Hoggar Mountains in the far south.

A population of around 48 million people, primarily identifying as Arab-Berber. Modern Standard Arabic and Tamazight are official language, with Algerian Arabic spoken daily and French widely used in administration and media. Sunni Islam is practiced by virtually the entire population, deeply shaping daily life and traditions. Home to significant civilizations, including Numidian kingdoms, Carthaginian trading ports, and exceptionally preserved Roman ruins like Timgad and Tipasa. Centuries of rich medieval Islamic dynasties followed by Ottoman governance shaped coastal architecture, including the famous Kasbah of Algiers. Gained independence in 1962 after a historic and challenging war, emerging as a proud, sovereign North African republic.

Thanks for sharing. I enjoyed watching Africa's biggest country.
